sn12.65:1.2: “Bhikkhus, before my enlightenment, while I was still a bodhisatta, not yet fully enlightened, it occurred to me:
sn12.65:1.3: ‘Alas, this world has fallen into trouble, in that it is born, ages, and dies, it passes away and is reborn,
sn12.65:1.4: yet it does not understand the escape from this suffering headed by aging-and-death.
sn12.65:1.5: When now will an escape be discerned from this suffering headed by aging-and-death?’
sn12.65:1.7: ‘When what exists does aging-and-death come to be? By what is aging-and-death conditioned?
sn12.65:1.8: ’ Then, bhikkhus, through careful attention, there took place in me a breakthrough by wisdom:
sn12.65:1.9: ‘When there is birth, aging-and-death comes to be; aging-and-death has birth as its condition.’
sn12.65:2.2: ‘When what exists does birth come to be?…
sn12.65:2.11: Then, bhikkhus, through careful attention, there took place in me a breakthrough by wisdom:
sn12.65:2.12: ‘When there is consciousness, name-and-form comes to be; name-and-form has consciousness as its condition.’
sn12.65:2.14: ‘When what exists does consciousness come to be? By what is consciousness conditioned?
sn12.65:2.15: ’ Then, bhikkhus, through careful attention, there took place in me a breakthrough by wisdom:
sn12.65:2.16: ‘When there is name-and-form, consciousness comes to be; consciousness has name-and-form as its condition.’
sn12.65:3.2: ‘This consciousness turns back; it does not go further than name-and-form.
sn12.65:3.3: It is to this extent that one may be born and age and die, pass away and be reborn, that is, when there is consciousness with name-and-form as its condition,
sn12.65:3.4: and name-and-form with consciousness as its condition.
sn12.65:3.5: With name-and-form as condition, the six sense bases;
sn12.65:3.6: with the six sense bases as condition, contact….
sn12.65:3.7: Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.’
sn12.65:3.8: “‘Origination, origination’—thus, bhikkhus, in regard to things unheard before there arose in me vision, knowledge, wisdom, true knowledge, and light.
sn12.65:4.2: ‘When what does not exist does aging-and-death not come to be?
sn12.65:4.3: With the cessation of what does the cessation of aging-and-death come about?’
sn12.65:4.4: Then, bhikkhus, through careful attention, there took place in me a breakthrough by wisdom:
sn12.65:4.5: ‘When there is no birth, aging-and-death does not come to be;
sn12.65:4.6: with the cessation of birth comes cessation of aging-and-death.’
sn12.65:4.8: ‘When what does not exist does birth not come to be?…
sn12.65:4.16: With the cessation of what does the cessation of name-and-form come about?’
sn12.65:4.17: Then, bhikkhus, through careful attention, there took place in me a breakthrough by wisdom:
sn12.65:4.18: ‘When there is no consciousness, name-and-form does not come to be;
sn12.65:4.19: with the cessation of consciousness comes cessation of name-and-form.’
sn12.65:5.2: ‘When what does not exist does consciousness not come to be?
sn12.65:5.3: With the cessation of what does the cessation of consciousness come about?’
sn12.65:5.4: Then, bhikkhus, through careful attention, there took place in me a breakthrough by wisdom:
sn12.65:5.5: ‘When there is no name-and-form, consciousness does not come to be;
sn12.65:5.6: with the cessation of name-and-form comes cessation of consciousness.’
sn12.65:6.2: ‘I have discovered this path to enlightenment, that is,
sn12.65:6.3: with the cessation of name-and-form comes cessation of consciousness;
sn12.65:6.4: with the cessation of consciousness comes cessation of name-and-form;
sn12.65:6.5: with the cessation of name-and-form, cessation of the six sense bases;
sn12.65:6.6: with the cessation of the six sense bases, cessation of contact….
sn12.65:6.7: Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.’
sn12.65:6.8: “‘Cessation, cessation’—thus, bhikkhus, in regard to things unheard before there arose in me vision, knowledge, wisdom, true knowledge, and light.
sn12.65:7.1: “Suppose, bhikkhus, a man wandering through a forest would see an ancient path, an ancient road travelled upon by people in the past.
sn12.65:7.3: He would follow it and would see an ancient city, an ancient capital that had been inhabited by people in the past, with parks, groves, ponds, and ramparts, a delightful place.
sn12.65:7.4: Then the man would inform the king or a royal minister:
sn12.65:7.5: ‘Sire, know that while wandering through the forest I saw an ancient path, an ancient road travelled upon by people in the past.
sn12.65:7.6: I followed it and saw an ancient city, an ancient capital that had been inhabited by people in the past, with parks, groves, ponds, and ramparts, a delightful place.
sn12.65:7.8: Then the king or the royal minister would renovate the city,
sn12.65:7.9: and some time later that city would become successful and prosperous, well populated, filled with people, attained to growth and expansion.
sn12.65:7.10: “So too, bhikkhus, I saw the ancient path, the ancient road travelled by the Perfectly Enlightened Ones of the past.
sn12.65:8.1: And what is that ancient path, that ancient road?
sn12.65:8.2: It is just this Noble Eightfold Path; that is,
sn12.65:8.3: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration.
sn12.65:8.5: I followed that path and by doing so I have directly known aging-and-death,
sn12.65:8.8: and the way leading to its cessation.
sn12.65:8.23: and the way leading to their cessation.
sn12.65:8.24: Having directly known them, I have explained them to the bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs, the male lay followers, and the female lay followers.
sn12.65:8.25: This holy life, bhikkhus, has become successful and prosperous, extended, popular, widespread, well proclaimed among devas and humans.”
